dockets.utility: New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (state rules)
dockets.what_it_says: Assembly Bill A5727, introduced 2026-10-29 by Assemblymen Myhre and Rumpf, would require the state's rules to authorize construction and operation of micro-reactors, defined as 20 MW or less. The authorization applies only once the NRC has approved the reactor's design. The bill amends the Power NJ Act, which already directs the Board of Public Utilities to authorize advanced reactors but does not name micro-reactors. The fetched text sets no cost-recovery or siting terms.
dockets.microreactor_read: A 1-20 MW buyer in New Jersey would get a state path only after NRC design approval.

items.headline: NRC issues construction permit for Dow and X-energy Texas plant
items.what_happened: The NRC issued a construction permit for the Long Mott Generating Station at Dow's Seadrift, Texas site. It covers four Xe-100 reactors each rated 80 MWe and 200 MWt. The source reports the permit as already issued and says the NRC's Final Safety Evaluation Report was released on 30 October. Dow has not made a final decision to build; it expects to consider a preliminary investment decision in 2027, and a separate operating licence is needed before fuel load.
items.why_it_matters: Each unit is 80 MWe, several times the top of a 1-20 MW buyer's range, so a small buyer gets no direct path from this permit. It does show a commercial advanced reactor clearing NRC construction review in this window.
items.binding_note: Permit issued, per the 2026-11-10 World Nuclear News report. The report does not state the issuance date, so the item date is the report date.
